With Beautiful Soup’s `html5lib` parser: ```python from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = '''

Paragraph 1

Paragraph 2

''' soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html5lib") for tag in soup.find_all("p"): print(tag.sourceline, tag.sourcepos, tag.string) ``` Output: ```text 2 0 Paragraph 1 3 16 Paragraph 2 ``` - `tag.sourceline` is the 1-based source line number. - `tag.sourcepos` is the position of the final character of the opening tag—the `>` character—within that line. - The position is zero-based. Thus, for: ```html

Paragraph 2

``` `sourcepos == 16` refers to the `>` in `

`. Beautiful Soup supports these properties with `html5lib` starting in version 4.8.1. You can disable tracking with: ```python BeautifulSoup(html, "html5lib", store_line_numbers=False) ``` In that case, the position values are `None`.
